extracted.intended_audience: trademark examiners, intellectual property office staff, trademark attorneys and other practitioners classifying or searching figurative trademark elements
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Vienna Classification (5th ed.) to code and search the figurative elements of trademarks: deciding which category/division/section a figurative element belongs to and how to record and publish the classification numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal purpose is practical: to facilitate trademark anticipation searches and to avoid reclassification work when documents are exchanged internationally under the Vienna Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 4 provides that the scope of the Classification is that attributed to it by each country party to the Agreement; the Classification does not bind countries regarding the extent of protection afforded to a mark. Countries may give the Classification legal scope beyond its administrative use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — hierarchical system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification is hierarchical and proceeds from the general to the particular by dividing figurative elements into categories, divisions and sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections are of two kinds: main sections and auxiliary sections. Every category, division and section has a number according to a special coding system (category 1–29, division 1–19, section 1–26). Vacant numbers are left for future additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding notation and formatting (CFE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended notation for reporting classification numbers: use the abbreviation 'CFE' followed by category.division.section numbers and a parenthetical edition number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and rules: write CFE 3.9.10,24,25 for Category 3 Division 9 Sections 10,24,25; use a dash for uninterrupted ranges (e.g., CFE 3.9.16-18); if section numbers are omitted write CFE 3.9. The Committee determined the abbreviation to be 'CFE'. Indicate edition as CFE (5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple category/division indications formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: When several categories/divisions are necessary for one registration, indicate each classification separately and in numerical order, separated by semicolons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CFE 1.1.2,10,25; 1.15.17; 2.9.1 (or CFE 1.1; 1.15; 2.9 if section numbers not included).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use in official documents and publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent offices of countries party to the Agreement are obliged to include the numbers of categories, divisions and sections in official documents and publications relating to registrations and renewals of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification numbers should be preceded by 'Classification of Figurative Elements' or 'CFE' (and indicate edition). National offices may reserve the right not to include numbers of all or some sections (Article 4(5)). Auxiliary sections (preceded by 'A') are not mandatory and may be used at national discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary sections: purpose and coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary sections group figurative elements already covered by main sections according to particular criteria to facilitate anticipation searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auxiliary sections are indicated in the list with an 'A' prefix, but the letter 'A' should not appear in the numerical code assigned to the figurative element at the time of coding. Use of auxiliary sections is discretionary for national offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and required skills for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent and correct classification (coding) and correct definition of search sections must be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such persons should be able to assess figurative elements according to their distinguishing properties; coding and search-definition are interdependent operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for first-time and ongoing users
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using the Classification, users must familiarize themselves with the Preface, Recommendations and General Notes, and must abide strictly by Explanatory Notes and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Classification is reproduced under three headings to aid decision-making: Table of Categories; Table of Categories and Divisions with Explanatory Notes; List of Categories, Divisions and Sections with Explanatory Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are non-binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of figurative elements in the publication are given for information only and do not form an integral part of the Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental rule — classification by shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Figurative elements should be placed in categories, divisions and sections on the basis of their shape, regardless of material composition or the purpose of the object in which they are incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: toys shaped as dolls/animals/vehicles follow the human/animal/vehicle categories respectively; pictures or sculptures are placed in the categories for the represented subject. Widely known pictures/sculptures should also be placed in division 22.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of an object forming part of another object
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of an object forming part of another object should be classified under the same category/division/section as the object of which it forms part, unless expressly classified elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: motor vehicle bodywork is placed with motor vehicles (18.1.7 and A18.1.9), whereas tyres, wheels or steering wheels are placed in parts-of-motor-vehicles section 18.1.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty — multiple classification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a figurative element is presented such that it is not possible to determine clearly whether it belongs to a given division or section, it should be placed in both divisions or sections unless a special note says otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a human representation cannot be clearly determined to be male or female, place it in both divisions 2.1 and 2.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite marks with multiple figurative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mark comprises several figurative elements each having distinctive characteristics and classified differently, place each figurative element in its appropriate categories/divisions/sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a bottle label showing a castle and a distinctive writing form should be placed in appropriate divisions/sections of categories 7 and 27; a man in uniform on horseback playing a trumpet is placed in sections 2.1.2, 2.1.20 and 2.1.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Notes — representation similarity rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation similar to an object or living creature mentioned in the text of a section is placed in that section even if not expressly mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of inscriptions and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Inscriptions representing a human being are to be placed in division 27.3; inscriptions in characters normally used in a given country are to be treated as word marks rather than classified under character-specific divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: punctuation marks representing beings/objects are included in 27.3; inscriptions in scripts normally used in a country should not be classified under 28 (inscriptions in various characters) as they constitute word marks in that country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories (1–29) — canonical list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification divides figurative elements into 29 named categories (e.g., 1: Celestial bodies; 2: Human beings; ... 29: Colours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 5th edition comprises 29 categories, 144 divisions, 775 main sections and 1,112 auxiliary sections. Each category entry in the Classification includes explanatory notes guiding placement in its divisions/sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 — Celestial bodies, natural phenomena, geographical maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes stars, comets, sun, earth/planets, moon, constellations, armillary spheres/planetaria, natural phenomena, geographical maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: stars indicating military rank included; suns represented solely as a disk without rays are placed in division 26.1 (geometrical figures). Auxiliary sections subdivide number/shape/combinations (e.g., A1.1.2 one star, A1.1.3 two stars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 — Human beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers men, women, children, mixed groups/scenes, parts of human body, skeletons, skulls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: inscriptions representing a human being are placed in 27.3; heads placed in appropriate divisions for men/women/children not in 2.9.25; groups that present as scenes go to division 2.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 — Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers quadrupeds (series I–V), parts of bodies, birds, aquatic animals, reptiles, insects, other animals and groups of animals classified in different divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: heads of quadrupeds are in appropriate divisions 3.1–3.5, not 3.6.25; written/typographical matter representing animals is classified under 27.3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 4 — Supernatural, fabulous, fantastic or unidentifiable beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes winged/horned personages, beings partly human/partly animal, fabulous animals, masks, and groups of figurative elements classified in different divisions of category 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: does not include human beings and fantastic animals composed of letters/figures (those go to 27.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5 — Plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes trees, bushes, leaves, branches, flowers, grain/seeds/fruits, vegetables, other plants, and decorations made of plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes indicate cross-classification exceptions (e.g., ornamental motifs composed of plants are in 5.13 or 25.1 depending).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 6 — Landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers mountains, rocks, grottoes, landscapes with water, desert/tropical landscapes, urban/village scenes, other landscapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: urban landscapes with water are classified in 6.7.11 (not in 6.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 7 — Constructions, advertisement structures, gates/barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes dwellings, buildings, advertisement hoardings/pillars, cages/kennels, parts of dwellings/interiors, monuments, stadiums, fountains, structural works, building materials, walls, gates, scaffolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 8 — Foodstuffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes bakers' products, pastry, confectionery, chocolate, milk/dairy/cheese, butchers' meat/pork/fish products and other foodstuffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 9 — Textiles, clothing, sewing accessories, headwear, footwear
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers textiles other than clothing, clothing (excluding headwear/footwear), sewing accessories/patterns, headwear, and footwear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes specify exclusions (e.g., headwear in 9.7, footwear in 9.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 10 — Tobacco, smokers' requisites, matches, travel goods, fans, toilet articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes tobacco and smokers' articles, travel goods/fans/bags, toilet articles/mirrors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 11 — Household utensils
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes knives/forks/spoons and kitchen utensils/machines, containers/plates/dishes/kitchen utensils for serving/preparing/cooking, and other household utensils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: excludes household utensils classified in categories 12, 13 or 19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 12 — Furniture, sanitary installations
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes furniture (including office furniture) and sanitary installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 13 — Lighting, wireless valves, heating/cooking/refrigerating equipment, washing/drying equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers lighting/wireless valves, heating/cooking/refrigerating equipment, washing machines and drying equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exclude certain electrical items classified elsewhere (e.g., electric lamps in 13 vs 16/17 as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 14 — Ironmongery, tools, ladders
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes tubes, cables, heavy ironmongery, small ironmongery articles, springs, keys/locks/padlocks, tools (including handles), agricultural/horticultural implements, ladders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include inclusion of representations of non-metallic ironmongery articles and exclusions of agricultural implements to 14.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 15 — Machinery, motors, engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers machines for industry/agriculture, motors/engines/industrial installations, machines for household use and office machines, wheels, bearings, electrical equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes show exclusions (e.g., household machines 15.3, office machines 15.5, electric lamps 13.1.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 16 — Telecommunications, sound recording/reproduction, computers, photography, cinematography, optics
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes telecommunications, sound recording/reproduction, computers and photography/cinematography/optics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 17 — Horological instruments, jewellery, weights and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers time-measuring instruments, jewellery, balances/weights, and measures (including calculating instruments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 18 — Transport, equipment for animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes land vehicles, equipment for animals, vehicles for use on water/amphibious vehicles, anchors, buoys, lifebelts, aerial/space vehicles, traffic signs and indicator boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exclude military tanks/aircraft/warships where classified elsewhere (18.1.14, 18.5.1, 18.3 respectively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 19 — Containers and packing, representations of miscellaneous products
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers large and small containers, bottles/flasks, parts/accessories of bottles, amphorae/pitchers/vases, receptacles for laboratory use/pharmacy, medical/surgical apparatus and miscellaneous product representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes define exclusions and include representations of products not classified elsewhere (e.g., coal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 20 — Writing, drawing/painting materials, office requisites, stationery and booksellers' goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes writing/drawing/painting materials and small office requisites, papers/documents, books/bookbindings/newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 21 — Games, toys, sporting articles, roundabouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers games and toys, sporting articles and roundabouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 22 — Musical instruments and their accessories, bells, pictures, sculptures
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes musical instruments, music accessories, bells, pictures and sculptures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: pictures or sculptures that are widely known and famous should also be placed in division 22.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 23 — Arms, ammunition, armour
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers side arms and other weapons (not firearms), firearms/ammunition/explosives, and armour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: excludes military tanks/aircraft/warships classified under transport (18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 24 — Heraldry, coins, emblems, symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes shields, seals/stamps, medals/coins/decorations, flags, crowns/diadems, emblems/insignia, crosses, arrows, signs/notations/symbols and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 25 — Ornamental motifs, surfaces or backgrounds with ornaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers ornamental motifs, horizontally elongated ornamental surfaces, backgrounds divided into two/four, surfaces or backgrounds covered with repeated figurative elements or inscriptions, and other ornamented surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes exclude ornamental motifs composed of plants (classified in 5.13) and elongated elliptical/triangular/quadrilateral surfaces (classified in 26.1/26.3/26.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 26 — Geometrical figures and solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes circles/ellipses, segments or sectors of circles/ellipses, triangles/lines forming an angle, quadrilaterals, other polygons, juxtaposed/joined/intersecting geometrical figures, lines/bands, other geometrical figures/indefinable designs, and geometrical solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include that geometrical figures composed of human beings/animals/plants/objects are included and inscriptions forming geometrical figures are in division 27.1. Many principal and auxiliary sections subdivide by composition (e.g., circles with inscriptions, circles containing animals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 27 — Forms of writing, numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers letters or numerals forming geometrical figures or typographical matter in perspective, letters/numerals representing human/animal/plant/object, letters or numerals presenting special forms of writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detailed auxiliary sections for letters in special forms (double outline, relief/shaded, embellished, monograms, signatures, letters linked to figurative elements), and rules for classification of punctuation marks representing beings/objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 28 — Inscriptions in various characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifies inscriptions according to script: Arabic, Chinese/Japanese, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew, Latin, historical/cuneiform/hieroglyphic, and other characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: in a given country, inscriptions in characters normally used there are considered word marks and not classified here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 29 — Colours
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifies colours and combinations (individual colours, two predominant colours, three, four, five and over, and auxiliary section for one predominant colour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sections list named colours (red/pink/orange, yellow/gold, green, blue, violet, white/grey/silver, brown, black) and aggregate colour classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: This document is the fifth edition of the Vienna Classification, entering into force January 1, 2003, and replaces previous editions; the Classification is periodically revised by the Committee of Experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should indicate the edition used (e.g., CFE (5)). The classification includes vacant numbers to permit future introduction of new divisions/sections; auxiliary sections and presentation changes (e.g., marking principal sections with an asterisk) were adopted by the Committee.
